title: I spent months building an autonomous Solana trading system — here’s BOONO actually running
author: Brave-Photograph9845
selftext:
I’ve been building BOONO for the past few months, mostly nights and weekends.

It’s an autonomous Solana trading system that discovers tokens, analyzes market + on-chain signals, scores them, applies risk gates, executes trades, manages positions and reconciles its state against the blockchain.

I recorded a short walkthrough of it actually running: scanner, live position, real-time P&L and bot controls.

The interesting part hasn’t really been “building a trading bot.” It’s been dealing with everything that goes wrong once real money and real market data are involved — stale prices, failed transactions, bad state, execution issues, risk controls, etc.

I’m considering opening more of BOONO to the community, so I’d genuinely like feedback from people who build trading systems / Solana infra.

What would you improve first?

comments.author: tradematesHQ
comments.body: The broker question is the first thing I'd nail down  -  execution quality and fee structure will eat your edge on Solana faster than any stale price issue. The failure modes you listed are the real product, honestly. Stale prices and failed txs are where most retail bots die, so your risk gates are probably the most valuable part of BOONO. On the scoring side, if you're not cross-checking your on-chain signals against broader market context, you're flying blind. Worth checking what trademates.co does with its 90-day investment score and action plans  -  it's a different angle on the same problem, scoring setups instead of tokens. What's your slippage tolerance on a failed tx retry, and are you tracking that as a cost?

replies.author: Brave-Photograph9845
replies.body:
No broker in the traditional sense. Jupiter handles routing, transactions are signed locally, then submitted through Helius or Jito depending on the execution path. Slippage is dynamic based on price impact and BOONO re-quotes right before signing. Failed/unconfirmed txs aren’t treated as fills, and actual execution data is taken from the confirmed on-chain transaction. Urgent exits have a separate, more aggressive path  
More info :

https://hamzabenjeddi.com/projects/boono-building-an-autonomous-trading-system-that-cant-lie-to-itself/
